facts.t: Appears in 2.03% of the 23,781 paintings in our archive (483 paintings, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 244).
In our 23,781-painting archive it is more common than 72% of the named colors.
Peaks in the 1900s: found in 2.0% of the 1,674 paintings we have from then (34 paintings). Against the same museums' baseline that is 1.9x the expected rate.
Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color (38% of the 244 paintings, by lightness rank within each painting, so varnish cannot fake it).
Most devoted painter: Paul Cezanne, in 8 of 50 works here (6.4x the baseline of the museums those works come from; as photographed 5.0x; n=8).

First seen in our archive in 1375 (aic-59843); the third-earliest painting is 1435, and the latest 1950 (392 dated paintings, at least 2% of the canvas, as photographed). The archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first.
Shares canvases with Deep Slate-Olive and Artichoke Green more than chance (lift 9.4 and 6.6; n=35 and 32).
In printed English the word peaks in the 2000s and rose fastest in the 1920s (Google Books, all senses of the word, so a color name that is also an object or a place can mislead).
